sanskrit: vidma te svapna janitraṃ pāpmanaḥ putro 'si yamasya karaṇaḥ | sa naḥ svapna suṣvapnyāt pāhi ||
english: We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of Sin, the instrument of Yama. May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.
We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of Greed [or Seizure]. [May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.]
We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of Nirṛti [Dissolution/Destruction]. [May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.]
We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of Ill-fortune. [May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.]
We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of Utter Ruin. [May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.]
We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of Complete Downfall. [May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.]

sanskrit: vidma te svapna janitraṃ devajāmīnāṃ putro 'si yamasya karaṇaḥ | sa naḥ svapna suṣvapnyāt pāhi ||
english: We know your birth, O Dream — you are the son of the divine kinswomen, the instrument of Yama. May that Dream protect us from evil dreaming.

sanskrit: ajaiṣmādyāsanāmādyābhūmānāgaso vayam | uṣo yasmād duṣvapnyād abhaiṣmāpa tad uccha | dviṣate tat parā vaha śapate tat parā vaha | yaṃ dviṣmo yaś ca no dveṣṭi tasmā enad gamayāmaḥ | uṣā devī vācā saṃvidānā vāg devī uṣasā saṃvidānā | uṣaspatir vācaspatinā saṃvidāno vācaspatir uṣaspatinā saṃvidānā | te 'muṣmai parā vahantv arāyān durṇāmnāḥ sadānvā rakṣāṃsi | kumbhīkā dūṣīkāḥ pīyakān | jāgradduṣvapnyaṃ svapneduṣvapnyam | anāgamiṣyato varān avitteḥ | saṃkalpān amucyā druhaḥ pāśāt | tad amuṣyāgne parā vahantu devā vadhrir yathāsad vithuro na sādhuḥ | tad asmai gamayāma iti ||
english: Today we have conquered, today we have prevailed, today we have become sinless. O Dawn, from whatever evil dream we feared — shine that away. Carry it away to the one who hates, carry it away to the one who curses. He whom we hate and he who hates us — to him we send this. The goddess Uṣas, in accord with Speech; the goddess Speech, in accord with Uṣas; the Lord of Dawn, in accord with the Lord of Speech; the Lord of Speech, in accord with the Lord of Dawn — may they carry away to that one the demons of ill omen, the evil-named, the ever-hunting rākṣasas, the kumbhīkās, the dūṣīkās, the pīyakas. The evil dream of the waking, the evil dream of the sleeping, the boons still to come, those not yet gained — freed from the snare of treachery, from the bonds of ill intent — may the gods carry all that away from him, O Agni, as the deafened one who is disordered is not upright. To him we send it, thus.

sanskrit: evānevāva sā garat | asau māṃ dveṣṭi sa ātmānaṃ dveṣṭu yo māṃ dveṣṭi sa ātmānaṃ dveṣṭu | nir dviṣantaṃ divo niṣ pṛthivyā nir antarikṣād bhajāma | suyāmaṃś cākṣuṣā | idam aham amum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putraṃ duṣvapnyād ava daye | yad adoado abhyagacchaṃ yad doṣā yat pūrvāṃ rātriṃ yad divā yan naktaṃ yaj jāgrato yat svapantaḥ | yad aharahar duṣvapnyam abhigacchāmi tasmād enam ava daye | taṃ jahi tena mandasva tasya pṛṣṭīr api śṛṇīhi taṃ prāṇo jahātu sa viprāṇo astu sa pra mīyatāṃ sa tato mā jīvīt ||
english: Even so, let that one be swallowed up. That one hates me — may he hate himself; whoever hates me, may he hate himself. We drive out the one who hates from the sky, from the earth, from the midair, with favorable rays of sight. I hereby release this son of so-and-so, the son of such-a-one, from evil dreaming. From whatever evil dream approached at twilight, at the first watch of night, by day, by night, in waking, in sleeping — from whatever evil dream I encounter day after day, from that I release him. Strike him down; rejoice in that; shatter his ribs; may his breath abandon him, may he be breathless, may he perish, may he not live henceforth.
